text:
Maya: quick canary results — repro during LLM-serve with batch=8 seq=2048. expandable_segments=true reduced hard OOMs but fragmentation went up
Liam: can you paste the allocation trace and config you used?
Maya: trace snippet:
```text
[GPU0] alloc 24MB slab id=3
[GPU0] free 24MB
[GPU0] alloc 1.2GB -> OOM
```
Maya: config used: `max_split_size_mb=64 garbage_collection_threshold=0.8 expandable_segments=1`
Nina: lowering max_split_size_mb to 16 or 8 tends to reduce large tail fragments. gc_threshold=0.6 is safer for steady-state
Liam: also try aligning buffer reuse to 256KB (buffer_reuse_alignment_kb=256) — tiny leftover fragments are killing reuse efficiency
Sam: FYI kernel selection change in last rollout forced aten -> cudnn matmul path which allocs an ephemeral workspace ~200MB per stream; that combined with big splits pushes us over
Maya: re-ran with max_split_size_mb=16, garbage_collection_threshold=0.6, buffer_reuse_alignment_kb=256, expandable_segments=0, expire_reuse_secs=30. 15-min canary: no OOMs, fragmentation down ~10 pct, token latency +8% p95 but stable
Nina: nice. can you paste perf snapshot (highwater / frag / kv cache unused)?
Maya: perf snapshot:
```json
{"gpu_mem_used_mb":"12288","gpu_mem_free_mb":"2560","fragmentation_pct":"18","kv_cache_unused_mb":"192","ephemeral_ws_mb":"210"}
```
Sam: kv_cache_unused ~200MB is actionable — warmup & prefix caching could reclaim that for workloads with steady prefixes
Liam: follow-up: try sticky-kernel-routing so hot traces hit the same kernel variant (reduces ephemeral workspace churn). Also consider lowering per-stream workspace limit in the kernel selector
Maya: starting a 2h run with sticky-kernel-routing + the smaller split + gc=0.6; will report back
infra-bot: deploying canary config `max_split_size_mb=16,gc_threshold=0.6,buffer_align_kb=256,sticky_kernel=on` to 6 hosts
infra-bot: canary live — monitoring redwood/oom/canary and redwood/latency/canary
Nina: if stable, propose default for p3dn-like fleets -> max_split_size_mb=16 and gc_threshold=0.6 in runtime defaults
Maya: agree. I'll draft PR with rollout and automated rollback (OOM spike >3 hosts)
Sam: tl;dr: lower max_split_size_mb + lower gc threshold + align reuse + sticky kernel routing. Watch kv cache warmup and kernel workspace
Liam: also add a short profiler harness to capture per-kernel workspace allocs during canary — saves time when diagnosing regressions
Maya: noted, will attach harness logs in PR
Nina: thanks all :thumbsup:
